idiom_name: asyncio.Future + dict keyed by correlation id + asyncio.wait_for
implementation_notes: asyncio.Future is the per-request reply channel: the caller creates a future, registers it under a fresh correlation id, publishes reply_to/correlation_id with the request, and awaits asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout) so a missing reply raises TimeoutError; the reply handler resolves the future, using loop.call_soon_threadsafe when the transport is threaded. Broker clients rebuild the same dict internally - the aio-pika RPC tutorial declares an exclusive callback queue, subscribes, and dispatches on_response by properties.correlation_id, and pika does the same with basic_consume.
code_sketch:
pending: dict[str, asyncio.Future[bytes]] = {}
async def call(payload: bytes, timeout: float = 5.0) -> bytes:
    corr = str(uuid.uuid4())
    fut = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
    pending[corr] = fut
    await publish(payload, reply_to=reply_queue, correlation_id=corr)
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(fut, timeout)   # TimeoutError if no reply
    finally:
        pending.pop(corr, None)                       # abandon on timeout/cancel
pitfalls: asyncio.wait_for cancels the future on timeout, so a reply arriving later raises InvalidStateError in the handler unless it checks fut.done() first.
Resolving the future from a pika consumer thread requires loop.call_soon_threadsafe; set_result from another thread is not thread-safe.
Entries that are not removed leak and make id reuse dangerous; treat unknown correlation ids as noise and log them.

variants.name: aio-pika RPC over an exclusive callback queue
variants.idiom_name: exclusive callback queue + on_response dispatch by correlation_id
variants.implementation_notes: The aio-pika and pika RPC patterns put the correlation table in the client library: declare an exclusive, auto-delete callback queue once, subscribe, publish with reply_to and correlation_id (or use RabbitMQ's direct reply-to pseudo-queue), and dispatch each delivery in the response callback to the future registered under properties.correlation_id. Choose it when requests must cross processes; the cost is a broker dependency plus the connection-recovery policy - a reconnected client gets a new callback queue and must re-declare it before any new request.
variants.code_sketch:
async def main():
    conn = await aio_pika.connect_robust(BROKER_URL)
    channel = await conn.channel()
    callback = await channel.declare_queue(exclusive=True)
    futures: dict[str, asyncio.Future] = {}
    async def on_response(message):
        fut = futures.pop(message.correlation_id, None)   # late/unknown: dropped
        if fut and not fut.done():
            await message.ack()
            fut.set_result(message.body)
pitfalls: An exclusive callback queue lives only as long as its connection: reconnection logic must re-declare it before any new request.
Acking automatically loses replies on failure; ack after resolving the future and make the handler idempotent for redeliveries.
